1.why: Every MFA route calls requireAuth → authenticatedSession, which resolves the session solely from the HttpOnly cookie and verifies session.accountId === account.id before any settings are read or changed.

2.why: Verification is bound to the single account's encrypted TOTP secret / recovery-code list and no user identifier is accepted from the request body (accountId/userId keys are rejected), so a code cannot validate for another account.

3.why: The /api/mfa/verify handler only sets account.mfaEnabled, updates acceptedCounter and clears failures — it never rotates the session id nor deletes other entries in the sessions map, so pre-existing sessions remain valid after enabling MFA.

4.why: account.encryptedSecret and account.encryptedRecoveryCodes are AES-256-GCM encrypted via encrypt() with a random IV and auth tag; plaintext is never persisted server-side.

5.why: Session ids, CSRF tokens, the 20-byte Base32 TOTP seed, IVs and recovery codes all derive from node:crypto randomBytes (only minor modulo bias in recoveryCode()).

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and the session cookie is HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, though the CSRF token, TOTP secret and OTP live in in-memory JS variables and are printed to the page/console.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validCode, decode32's charset check) plus content-type/length checks and rejection of unexpected keys gate every request; no SQL/string-built queries exist.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted with textContent/createTextNode/replaceChildren (innerHTML only ever receives static literals) and a strict nonce-based CSP with object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' is served.

9.why: The application contains no redirect logic at all (no Location headers or 30x responses), so while there is no open-redirect risk, no allow-list of internal destinations actually exists.

10.why: headers() sets Strict-Transport-Security, a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

11.why: cookie()/clearCookie() emit mfa_session with Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict and a bounded Max-Age.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces and tokens never appear in URLs, but /api/mfa/setup returns the TOTP seed and a live testOtp which the client writes to console.log and an on-page log panel, along with all recovery codes.

13.why: TOTP acceptance is limited to a ±1 30-second window and replay is blocked by requiring found > acceptedCounter, while recovery codes are spliced out on use and carry a 30-day expiresAt that is checked.

14.why: failed()/locked() count failures per account and impose a 10-minute lockout after 5 failures, returning HTTP 429 for both OTP and recovery-code verification.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the pre-auth session and issues a brand-new id and CSRF token, sessions enforce 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute expiry, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
